videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

videos.title: VoiceOver: ¿Esa voz es nueva?
videos.description:
VoiceOver no tiene por qué quedarse únicamente con las voces que trae el iPhone.
En este vídeo pruebo dos formas de ampliar su repertorio: las voces de Visionauta, una aplicación de reconocimiento del entorno que permite incorporarlas al sistema, y Runa TTS, una nueva plataforma que todavía se encuentra en fase beta y no está disponible en la App Store.
Escucharemos cómo suenan y qué posibilidades ofrecen para darle a VoiceOver un registro diferente.

videos.title: Un ciego prevenido vale por dos: alertas sísmicas en el móvil
videos.description:
En este vídeo hablo de algo que ojalá no tengamos que necesitar nunca, pero que conviene conocer: cómo puede ayudarnos el móvil a recibir avisos relacionados con terremotos.
Primero explico qué opciones existen en Android y en iPhone para recibir alertas en tiempo real cuando hay un terremoto cerca, siempre dependiendo del país, la cobertura y los sistemas oficiales disponibles.
Después presento una aplicación llamada Earthquake, disponible para iPhone y Android, que permite hacer seguimiento de movimientos sísmicos, consultar información sobre terremotos, avisos de tsunami y otros datos útiles. La app se puede usar con VoiceOver y puede resultar interesante para quienes quieran estar informados desde el móvil de forma accesible.
No se trata de vivir con miedo, sino de saber qué herramientas tenemos a mano cuando la tierra decide moverse sin pedir permiso.

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan

Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.

news.title: What's the difference between Android Automotive and Google Built-In?
news.summary: One is a set of apps while the other can run almost everything inside of a car.
news.body:
One is a set of apps while the other can run almost everything inside of a car.

Despite the popularity of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, car manufacturers are moving away from these phone mirroring applications in favor of native infotainment systems. Google, for its part, has supported this transition through Android Automotive and Google Built-in, two in-car infotainment software stacks that place Android's popular OS into your car. For instance, GM has moved away from Android Auto in favor of a Google Built-in solution since 2023. Automakers tout such moves as bringing a more seamless connection between a driver and their vehicle. But some customers continue to meet these changes with a mix of anger and confusion, with some lamenting that built-in systems are likely intended to open new revenue streams, either through subscription models or the sale of driver data, rather than provide a better driving experience.

Google has grown into a major player in this swiftly-changing infotainment space. Manufacturers deploy the Mount View company's in-car technology through two operating systems, Android Automotive Operating System (AAOS) and Google Built-in. Unlike phone mirroring applications like Android Auto, which simply project your phone's display onto your car's dashboard, both Android Automotive and Google Built-in are independent operating systems, complete with applications and features that run without your phone. And while connecting your phone and car to the same Google account may increase compatibility, neither requires its driver to use an Android phone. For most consumers, parsing the differences between Android Automotive and Google Built-in can be difficult. However, the distinction presents measurable changes in the customer experience, and can have a major effect on how your infotainment system looks and operates.

Android Automotive is a full-stack software solution that car manufacturers integrate into their cars' systems to operate their radio, climate control, cameras, mirrors, lighting, seat adjustments and instrument clusters. Open source and highly customizable, manufacturers design their own in-vehicle infotainment and software systems using Google's infotainment architecture. This added flexibility is key, as manufacturers can create systems specific to their brands and drivers, adding Android in-house applications and customizing layouts as they see fit. In some instances, drivers may not even be aware that their infotainment system is powered by Google. Rivian, for instance, declines to include Google-specific branding in its Android Automotive system despite relying on the open source architecture for its Rivian OS infotainment system.

Google Built-in, on the other hand, is a group of applications that manufacturers license to integrate into their Android automotive systems. Debuted in 2020, Google Built-in allows drivers to access applications like Google Maps and Gemini. Manufacturers that license Google Built-in also give their customers access to Google Play Store, where they can access popular media applications like Spotify, YouTube, and Google Play. As it stands, sixteen brands have access to Google Built-in, including Honda, Volvo, Chevy, Nissan, Ford, BYD, and Renault. For a full list, visit Google's Built-in website .

The differences between Google Built-in and Google Automotive Services may get more pronounced as Google accelerates its incorporation of advanced AI features into its Google Built-in applications. Rolled out across sixteen car brands, Gemini is officially replacing Google Assistant as the infotainment system's go-to chatbot passenger.

Billed by some proponents as Gemini at its most practical , the integration of Google's flagship chatbot into its Google Built-in car suite brings a host of voice-activated AI features into your car's cockpit. One of the greatest leaps is its Google Maps application, which will now incorporate real-time traffic updates, EV-tailored routing, and Gemini's smart navigations. Drivers will also be able to use Gemini to check their email and messages, craft playlists and even order dinner. One feature touted by Google is Gemini Live, a feature in which you can chat with Gemini about your destination. Gemini Live can even tap into your car's front facing camera, just incase you really need your car to pontificate about what is directly in front of you. Drivers can also adjust in-car settings, access hard to find settings and gain insights into their car's battery or performance metrics.

Google's rollout of Gemini initiated earlier this summer, premiering with cars that support the company's phone mirroring application, Android Auto, before rolling out to popular brands with Google Built-in like Honda, Chevrolet and Volvo.

Some Google customers, like Ford and Rivian, have instead invested in developing their own AI assistants. GM, meanwhile, is reportedly splitting the difference, both introducing Gemini to its Google Built-in software system while reportedly developing its own proprietary in-vehicle AI, set to release later this year. As GM executive Anna Santos told CNBC , the assistant will use "GM vehicle knowledge and OnStar intelligence" to "go beyond what a general purpose assistant can do." The dual-track approach reflects the broader infotainment landscape, in which many manufacturers race to incorporate AI into their vehicles while simultaneously developing homegrown agents. How these shifts change Google's approach to in-car software system will be a major question moving forward.

news.title: What is the oldest Samsung device that still gets software updates in 2026?
news.summary: Knowing how long your phone will get updates is important for deciding when to upgrade.
news.body:
Knowing how long your phone will get updates is important for deciding when to upgrade.

Android 17 brought several productivity-focused improvements to smartphones this year. Naturally, the latest devices will support future updates for at least a couple of years. But if you have a Samsung device that's inching toward its proverbial "end of life," you may want to know if your phone will keep getting updates. Samsung has already shipped Android 17-based One UI 9 on devices like the Galaxy Fold 8 series and the Flip 8.

While security updates are commonly sent to phones well past their prime, software updates that bring meaningful changes aren't as common. That goes double for Samsung's affordable A series. Longer support periods from smartphone makers are a relatively new trend, meaning older-generation phones don't share that kind of longevity and may already be out of support.

Keeping track of how long a phone will be supported is essential when you're deciding to hold on to an existing phone or purchase a new one. Here's what you need to know about which phones Samsung hasn't abandoned just yet, from flagships to budget phones.

How long a Samsung smartphone receives Android updates depends on the device's tier. Flagships enjoy up to 7 years of support while mid-range devices get about 5-6 years. Budget models get up to 4 years of support.

Here are the Samsung phones that still get Android updates in 2026:

Samsung's Galaxy A34 gets these updates until March 2027. The A54 5G will get Android updates until March 2027, while the A73 no longer gets them as of April 2026.

And here are the Samsung tablets that continue to get Android updates in 2026:

The Galaxy Tab Active 5 receives Android updates until January 2028, while the Active 5 Pro gets them until 2033.

These Samsung wearables will continue to get updates this year:

Manufacturers don't warn you before cutting you off from software and security updates. You'll have to look up your smartphone model online to verify. Samsung has a handy security update list you can check. If you go into your Settings app and find that your phone hasn't been updated in several months or years, chances are that your phone isn't supported anymore.

That bargain on a refurbished model you spotted online might be moot if it loses access to updates within the year. Lose security patches, and your phone becomes vulnerable to all sorts of new threats from hackers.

As your phone misses out on more updates, apps slowly become incompatible if they're designed with the latest OS versions in mind. Worse, strange popups and apps that appear without warning and guzzle your internet data might mean your device has been hacked. These are clear signs that you're due for a new phone.

news.title: MacBook Pro overhaul: entry-level model to gain new design sooner than expected
news.summary: Earlier this year, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman revealed that Apple has a new M7-powered entry level MacBook Pro in the pipeline for spring 2027. This isn’t an ordinary MacBook Pro refresh though. It’ll bring the upcoming redesign down to the entry level, something that previously wasn’t expected. more…
news.body:
Earlier this year, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman revealed that Apple has a new M7-powered entry level MacBook Pro in the pipeline for spring 2027. This isn’t an ordinary MacBook Pro refresh though. It’ll bring the upcoming redesign down to the entry level, something that previously wasn’t expected.

Normally, when Apple introduces a new MacBook Pro design, it takes a while to trickle down. For instance, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M1 Pro and M1 Max was introduced in 2021, but the base model MacBook Pro stuck with the 13-inch design until 2023, when it gained the 14-inch chassis with the M3 chip .

Similarly, when Apple redesigned the MacBook Pro in 2016, it wasn’t until 2019 that the entry level model gained the Touch Bar. There’s also a similar story for the 2012 retina MacBook Pro redesign.

This time around though, there’ll only be a roughly 6 month gap before the redesign comes to the entry level.

According to Bloomberg , Apple will be introducing the redesign to the entry level MacBook Pro in early 2027, shortly after debuting it in the high end MacBook Pros, rumored to be called MacBook Ultra. From the report :

Apple is also preparing a revamped entry-level MacBook Pro, code-named K104, for as early as the first half of next year. The 14-inch laptop will adopt a new design in line with what Apple is preparing for higher-end MacBooks with touch screens due between the end of this year and early next year.

It’s worth noting that there’ll also be another entry level MacBook Pro with the current design and the M6 chip, which is currently on track to debut this fall alongside the redesigned high-end MacBook Pros.

To make things even weirder, those redesigned high-end MacBook Pros are also expected to debut with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, instead of M6 generation chips. Apple recently made a decision to abandon its plans for high end M6 chips to instead accelerate M7.

In short, it’ll look like this:

Of course, the redesign is expected to feature a slightly thinner chassis, OLED displays with touch support, and possibly even come with a Dynamic Island.

With the recent price hikes, this is excellent news for some people. I’m sure the redesigned 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro will likely cost over $2500, so if you’re looking to get something more in budget with the M7 chip and the redesign, you’ll only have to wait until the following spring.

It’s certainly unfortunate that the $1,999 price point of the entry level MacBook Pro today is what the Pro chip versions cost just under a year ago , but that’s the inevitable reality of this memory shortage .

Are you looking forward to the M7 MacBook Pro with the redesign? Let us know in the comments.

news.title: How to enable Live Activities on iPhone and CarPlay
news.summary: Live Activities put the most important real-time information from apps in a place where it's easy to keep an eye on.
news.body:
Keep track of important updates without having to open the app every two minutes.

At a time when most Android phones had already switched to tiny hole-punch cutouts to house their front-facing cameras, the iPhone 14 Pro launched with a long pill-shaped cutout. Apple has used this as its standard since then, aside from the budget "e" phones and iPhone Duo, and even made it smaller for the iPhone 18 Pro series .

This is because iPhones pack more than just a camera inside the cutout; there are additional sensors required for Face ID to work. Instead of hiding the pill with cleverly designed wallpapers, Apple leaned into it with the Dynamic Island , using the surrounding area to turn an otherwise awkward design constraint into a useful part of the iOS experience.

Your iPhone's Live Activities show up on the Dynamic Island when using your phone. They display information you might want to keep an eye on without having to constantly switch back to the associated app: timers, navigation directions, music playback and sports scores can be displayed as Live Activities. Many third-party apps like food delivery and flight tracking services have also adapted to use the Dynamic Island.

Live Activities should be enabled by default, but if you don't see them for certain apps, check if they've accidentally been turned off. On your iPhone, navigate to Settings > Apps and select any app that's been giving you trouble. Make sure the Live Activities slider is enabled. Though Live Activities work independently of regular notifications, you might want to also enable notifications for the app if you're not seeing the expected updates.

These activities will also appear on the Lock screen when you're not using your device. To make sure this is enabled, visit Settings > Face ID & Passcode . Confirm your passcode, then scroll down to the Allow Access When Locked section and be sure Live Activities is on.

CarPlay makes it easy to access vital info from your iPhone without getting too distracted while driving. As part of this, it can display Live Activities so you can track the status of a food delivery or updates for an upcoming flight.

Live Activities from your iPhone are automatically displayed on the CarPlay Dashboard, the split-screen view to the left of your app list. If you're using an app that covers the entire screen, Live Activities will still be shown as notifications at the bottom of the display. If they become too distracting, you can always turn the feature off in CarPlay or disable Live Activities for specific noisy apps, as above.

In case you're not seeing them, open the Settings app in CarPlay, scroll down and make sure the Live Activities toggle is enabled. You should also confirm the Suggestions in CarPlay (or Suggestions in Dashboard ) option is turned on. If they still don't appear, try turning off Driving Focus if it's running.

Besides this, you can add widgets to CarPlay for quick controls and information from apps without having to open them. Widgets live in the leftmost section of the CarPlay Dashboard. Spend a little more time in the Settings app, and you'll discover more ways to customize how CarPlay looks on your car's display .

news.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
news.summary: In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
news.body:
Posted:

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved.

In a Saturday morning post on X , Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.

“We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI .

As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”

“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said. “Think of it like an emergency brake.”

Nadella’s comments come as leading AI companies acknowledge more and more incidents where they seemed to lose control of their models , and after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan for more cautious AI development.

news.title: Amazon’s new Alexa Tablet finally gives the iPad lineup some much needed competition
news.summary: This week, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa Tablets. They no longer run a proprietary OS with a custom App Store, and instead embrace Android with a stock feel – while offering the Play Store. It’s a big shift in direction for Amazon. The tablets also look quite beautiful, while previous Fire tablets have felt cheap. I think these have the opportunity to do quite well. more…
news.body:
This week, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa Tablets . They no longer run a proprietary OS with a custom App Store, and instead embrace Android with a stock feel – while offering the Play Store. It’s a big shift in direction for Amazon. The tablets also look quite beautiful, while previous Fire tablets have felt cheap. I think these have the opportunity to do quite well.

First and foremost, I want to make it quite clear that I’m not saying the iPad is doomed or anything remotely close to that. However, I do think the Alexa Tablet serves as a real form of iPad competition, which the iPad has generally lacked.

Amazon is putting a lot of care into these tablets that other Android manufacturers haven’t, and while these tablets come in at lower price points – they certainly punch above their weight class.

There are three Alexa Tablets to start off the lineup: an 8.7” model at $229 , an 11” model at $329 , and a 12” Pro model at $499 . To me, the one in the middle is the most interesting.

It offers 8GB of RAM, a 90Hz display, a thin design, and a similarly sharp display. That compares to the budget iPad , which comes in $120 higher with less RAM, a lesser display, and a thicker design. Granted, the iPad has the A16 chip, which probably feels much faster than the MediaTek chip powering it. The iPad also starts at 128GB, compared to the 64GB on the Alexa Tablet . Once you upgrade the Alexa Tablet to 128GB , there’s only a $70 difference.

Hardware wise, the Alexa Tablets seem pretty competent. Obviously, Android on tablets isn’t going to be quite perfect, but given its tie in with Alexa and the fact that the tablet is priced quite well, I could see a lot of people wanting to buy these, even if they potentially would’ve considered iPads . Of course, one strong suit from Amazon is the Kindle experience, and these Alexa Tablets offer a reader mode that cuts blue light.

Only time will tell, but Amazon might make a pretty big dent into the tablet market with its new entries. Even the 12” Pro at $499 seems like a really worthwhile product. At the very least, I hope some strong competition means Apple will be less complacent with its iPad upgrades. For example, the iPad Air has largely only received chip upgrades since its last redesign in 2020.

I’m personally excited to try one of these out and truly put it to the test. Right now, Amazon also offers 20% off with any trade-in , making it an even better deal.

What do you think of these new Alexa Tablets ? Would you consider getting one of these for a friend or family member during the holiday season? Sound off in the comments.

news.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
news.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
news.body:
Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.

While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.

Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.

For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026.

Comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished.

Completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies users and recommends the next steps.

It can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. Comma maintains context and memory across devices and conversations, and can deliver daily briefings, flag urgent matters, and summarize recorded calls.

Comma is free to start and open source.

Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized plan.

The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar.

Fambot currently connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with support for Apple Calendar planned for the future.

The company launched in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is currently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription.

Folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations.

One distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally.

Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background.

Instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion , valuing it at $10 billion.

The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. Users can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The company says early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and canceling subscriptions.

In September, Instinct began giving users dedicated email addresses for their assistants. The idea is to let Instinct create and manage accounts on a user’s behalf without filling the user’s personal inbox. The agent can use its address to sign up for services, contact businesses, follow up on requests, and handle tasks that require an email account. (However, this level of autonomy has also raised concerns about privacy and security .) It’s also begun rolling out support for placing calls .

The company remains in private beta.

Powered by Hermes Agent, Iris is designed to let users delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request.

Martin is a general-purpose personal assistant reachable through SMS as well as phone, WhatsApp, email, Slack, and its own iOS app.

It can help manage calendars, email, reminders, tasks, notes, and communications. It can also act on behalf of users by sending messages or making phone calls, while providing daily summaries of what needs attention.

It’s a bit on the pricier side, with subscriptions starting at $21 per month.

Miso takes the personal-assistant concept and applies it specifically to travel.

It operates through iMessage and combines AI trip planning with support from a dedicated travel team. Users can arrange flights through messaging while Miso takes into account their travel preferences, loyalty points, and other priorities. Miso also gives travelers access to trip details and flight updates, along with personalized recommendations.

Ohai is another family assistant focused on helping households manage the constant stream of information and tasks involved in everyday family life.

Users can send messages, forward emails, or make voice requests, and the assistant can transform them into schedules, reminders, and plans. It can also coordinate calendars, household chores, and meals across multiple members of a family.

It includes a free basic option, but also offers different subscriptions based on family size, starting at $9.99 per month.

Similar to the other family-focused agents, the idea behind Ollie is that families already have the information they need, but it lives across school messages, calendars, task lists, and group chats. Ollie aims to bring those pieces together and keep them in sync. It can keep track of calendars, emails, reminders, tasks, and other household details, then deliver relevant information to users through text.

Its biggest differentiator from other agents is that Ollie is one of the first mainstream, family-focused AI assistants to achieve SOC 2 compliance, a widely used security standard.

Launched in June 2026, Ollie offers a free tier, as well as paid plans starting at $25 per month for 150 messages. A $100-per-month plan includes up to 1,000 messages.

Orbits also has an AI assistant that is focused on the household.

It works through both the Orbits app and text messaging, and can bring together calendars, lists, and conversations while also carrying out tasks for you. That can include searching the web, making purchases, booking restaurants, changing appointments, and requesting quotes for household services.

Additionally, Orbits can remind family members about chores, communicate with service providers, and help coordinate responsibilities beyond the immediate household.

Orbits is backed by investors like Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Speedrun fund, N49P, and Garage Capital.

Users can interact with Pally as they would with a friend while giving it access to the apps they already rely on. The assistant can connect information spread across services such as WhatsApp, Gmail, calendars, and Google Drive, helping users keep track of plans, receipts, dates, files, and other details.

There’s a free plan available, which offers features like 15 minutes of calls per month, or there are paid plans, including $25 per month for 30 minutes of calls and $100 per month for 60 minutes.

Poke launched in March 2026 as a general-purpose assistant that you can reach through text messaging. It can handle tasks involving calendars, planning, health and fitness, smart-home controls, photos, and other everyday activities.

Poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform. A month later, parent company The Interaction Company of California was acquired by AI coding startup Cognition in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

Rene is an AI personal assistant designed to be a user’s “best contact” rather than another productivity agent. It’s text-based and can turn natural-language conversations into tasks, reminders, summaries, and other follow-up actions. Rene also maintains context across conversations, allowing it to remember details and surface things that may need attention later.

Additionally, it has a browser, can write code, shop for you, as well as create slides and images.

Rene is currently available on iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Instead of waiting for users to open an app, Skye is an “ agentic homescreen ” for the iPhone that analyzes information from connected services and surfaces what it thinks is relevant through contextual cards, suggestions, and daily briefings. The assistant can generate audio briefings, prepare information ahead of meetings, surface reminders, and identify potentially useful information.

The company, Signull Labs, raised about $3.6 million in seed funding in 2025. It entered private testing and beta in April 2026, and hasn’t yet announced a public release date.

Stanley is an AI content assistant aimed at content creators rather than general personal productivity. Available through iMessage, Telegram, and the web, it acts as a kind of AI head of content, helping users come up with ideas, turn them into posts, and maintain a consistent publishing schedule.

For instance, Stanley can connect to a user’s Instagram account, using that context to suggest content based on what the user has actually been doing. Users can also send voice notes, which Stanley turns into scripts, captions, and other social assets. It includes a content calendar and can schedule posts, with the broader goal of making content creation a more continuous, automated process rather than something users have to sit down and plan from scratch.

Szn is designed to coordinate tasks and follow-ups through a single conversation thread. Users can send text messages, voice notes, photos, or forwarded emails, and the assistant takes action on their behalf, including making calls, sending emails, and managing follow-ups.

According to the company’s website, Szn has served more than 7,500 businesses across 16 countries, completed over 10,000 jobs, and handled 95 hours of calls.

Tab allows users to delegate everyday tasks through familiar messaging platforms. Users can send requests to the assistant via iMessage or WhatsApp, ranging from ordering groceries to finding birthday gifts, and Tab handles the process on their behalf.

The company emerged from stealth in early October with a valuation of $300 million. Its investors include SV Angel, Valar Ventures, and American Spirit.

The biggest differentiator with Tomo ’s personal assistant for iMessage is that, instead of being a private assistant that only you interact with, Tomo can become part of group conversations.

Also, like other agents, it’s designed to help with goals, accountability, scheduling, and everyday organization. It also has the ability to send reminders, search the web, work with calendars and email, watch videos, and edit photos.

The basic plan starts at $19.99 per month.

Town is aimed more at professional life. It gives users a “Townie,” an AI assistant designed to learn how they work and handle recurring professional tasks. It can work with email, calendars, documents, Slack, and other platforms.

In June 2026, the company raised a $55 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner.

Underdog is a privacy-focused AI assistant that launched an invite-only beta in early October 2026. Unlike cloud-based AI services, the model runs entirely on the user’s device, keeping personal data on hardware they already own. The initial release supports Mac and Windows computers, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions planned for the future.

The company plans to offer the app for free initially and has stated that it will never include advertising.

Wajo ’s first consumer agent, Fo, can call businesses, send emails, join group chats, make bookings and purchases, and coordinate with people to complete everyday tasks.

A key part of Wajo’s approach is giving Fo its own identity. The agent has its own email address, phone number, and payment card, allowing it to interact with businesses without requiring users to hand over their own credentials.

Notably, when Fo encounters something it cannot handle on its own, Wajo says it can bring in a human assistant to finish the task.

Fo launched publicly in September 2026 with a free tier, while heavier workloads and custom agents are available through a paid Pro offering.

Apple @ Work is exclusively brought to you by Mosyle , the only Apple Unified Platform. Typically, Apple’s fall updates for IT are around better way to manage devices, etc. This year, there was an underrated update that I think will be a real win in certain situations: remote AppleCare log collection .

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

If you’ve ever opened an AppleCare support case for a hard-to-reproduce issue in your Apple fleet, you know how hard this process is. AppleCare needed a sysdiagnose and getting one meant either physically having the device or walking a user through a series of steps they’ve never done before. That process worked eventually, but it was slow, required the user to be available and willing to help, and, for remote employees or traveling executives, made it appear that IT didn’t have sufficient visibility into the logs of what was happening on the devices. The issue is that they somewhat didn’t.

The harder the issue was to reproduce, the more frustrating this was for IT. By the time you got the logs, the device had rebooted, the macOS state had changed, and you were starting over with your troubleshooting.

Apple introduced two new device management commands in iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS 27: TriggerEnhancedLogCollection and a cancel command. The process is straightforward. You open an AppleCare case, AppleCare provides you a token, and you pass that token through your device management when you trigger the command. The device collects the logs and uploads them directly to Apple, where they are automatically attached to the ticket with Apple.

The device also reports its status through declarative management at all times, so you can see whether log collection has started, whether it’s finished, whether it’s waiting on user consent, and if the upload is in progress.

There are two modes for this command, and the difference matters depending on what you’re managing. On iOS, non-interactive mode is available when the device has no passcode and no accounts, so it collects and uploads logs in the background without user involvement. I think this would be applicable in kiosk/POS type settings. On tvOS and Shared iPads, non-interactive is always available.

On macOS, interactive mode is required. The user sees a notification and is prompted to consent to both the log collection and the upload. They can decline, but this is still dramatically better than the old process, but it’s not completely hands-off. The user is in the loop., but at least it’s a simple UI box..

Remote and hybrid work make manual log collection harder and a remote user in a different city experiencing intermittent macOS issues is one of the more challenging support scenarios an IT team can face. With this feature, the moment that Apple’s team asks for logs, you can send the command from your device management console, the device does the work, and Apple has the info it needs to work the case.

news.title: ArcFlush: Roguelike Solitaire
news.summary: Cards don't line up politely here. They're stacked in layers — the way mahjong tiles are stacked, except these are playing cards, and one of the maps is on fire. Which means there are two games sitting on top of each other: getting a card out of the pile, and knowing what to do with it once you have it. HOW IT WORKS · The map is a layered formation. Anything underneath is locked until you clear what's covering it, so every card you take decides what you're allowed to take next. That half is solitaire. · Play up to five of the cards you've taken as a poker hand. A pair is fine. A Flush is better. A Straight Flush means you planned ahead — or got lucky and will claim you planned ahead. That half is poker. · Beat the stage's target score, spend what you earned in the Shop, and do it again. And again. Until the target has grown a couple of digits and you're no longer certain which of your trinkets is doing the heavy lifting. WHAT'S IN IT · Every map is built around exactly one idea. Ice Lake freezes cards. Furnace sets them alight. Dark Pool turns the lights off and invites you to feel your way out. · Clear a map and its Twist unlocks: the same map, in a considerably worse mood. · Trinkets. Some add points. Some quietly rewrite a rule you'd assumed was permanent. The legendary ones turn up rarely enough that finding the right one feels like the run has decided to help you, just this once. · A Shop between stages, because a roguelite without a shop is just a difficult puzzle. · A tutorial that leaves quickly and waits in Settings in case you ever want it back. WHAT'S NOT IN IT · Ads. · In-app purchases. · A season pass, a battle pass, or a little bar that refills while you sleep. · An internet connection. This app has never phoned home and wouldn't know who to call. Buy it once and own all of it — every map, every trinket, every Twist. There is nothing else to sell you, and we are not going to think of anything. One deck, thirteen languages. Good luck.

news.title: Anthropic can’t reliably control its AI agents. It’s cutting off its internal evals from the live internet instead
news.summary: Anthropic said it "turned off live internet access" for "all our internal evaluations" until further notice.
news.body:
Anthropic said its models exploited websites on the internet, including some run by U.S. government agencies, and it will turn off live internet access for all of its internal evaluations until the frontier lab is sure it can monitor and control its AI agents.

The incidents, disclosed in a blog post , involved AI agents tasked to solve problems seeking resources on the internet. In the process, they exploited software flaws, accessed databases without paying fees, used URL shortening services to smuggle information past restrictions, and even submitted a false murder tip to the Philadelphia police.

Anthropic said it discovered these new issues in a review of its model’s activities that began in July, demonstrating the lab’s lack of awareness of its software’s behavior in real time.

Notably, the company said that alignment training was not yet sufficient for skills like search and computer use that are central to its pitch that AI agents will be used by any professional who relies on digital tools.

The behaviors Anthropic disclosed are similar to incidents involving OpenAI agents that collaborated to break into various websites in search of information, including some run by the Australian government.

Anthropic previously disclosed that its models had broken into external systems. The frontier lab said it considered today’s disclosures “significantly less severe from an alignment and security perspective” than those it announced before.

However, the lab still said it had “turned off live internet access” for “all our internal evaluations” until it is certain it can monitor and control its agents.

It’s not clear what that means. Sydney Von Arx, the founder of Nightingale, an AI safety organization, told TechCrunch in an interview before this disclosure that developing models on a data center cut off from the open internet would be very challenging for researchers, and hinder the progress of the models, which benefit from internet access.

“You have to align them at some point,” Von Arx said. “If the AIs are released to production and never have access to the internet, that’s not a very useful tool.”

Anthropic said the behavior was a result of flaws in the lab’s training environments, which led the models to believe they would be rewarded for finding loopholes or avoiding restrictions, a behavior called “reward hacking.”

The company said it would stop running some of its evaluations or move them offline, and has built tooling to detect and block this behavior. This tooling was tested against the kind of incidents disclosed today and blocked them; it’s not clear what evidence will prompt Anthropic to return live internet access to its internal evaluations. Anthropic also said it would migrate its internal AI agents to “centrally managed infrastructure with strong containment,” and is beginning to using safety classifiers more frequently to monitor those agents.

“It’s encouraging that Anthropic voluntarily disclosed more recent incidents, including where their agents targeted U.S. government websites,” Conrad Stosz, an official at AI oversight lab Transluce and former head of the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation, said in a statement. “But it just underscores the need for independent, credible, third-party verification of Al systems. Trust in this technology needs to be built through science-backed oversight and governance with meaningful access — not by relying on researchers to find these things in the wild or on companies to voluntarily disclose.”

news.title: Ukraine’s drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia’s Google"
news.summary: One damaged data center has supercomputers used for training Yandex’s AI model.
news.body:
Ukrainian drone strikes have knocked out two of five data centers belonging to the Russian tech giant Yandex. The damage has left Yandex, known as “Russia’s Google” because it operates the country’s most popular search engine, struggling to maintain its AI chatbot and other online services.

The Ukrainian drones struck Yandex data centers in the Sasovo and Kaluga regions of Russia on October 8 and October 9, according to Reuters . Those actions came as a direct response to a Russian drone strike campaign targeting Ukraine’s data centers , which has disrupted mobile phone and Internet services for thousands of Ukrainians since late September.

“We continue to respond to Russia’s attacks on Ukraine, and we’re doing so with high precision,” said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a post on X. “Another data center was hit as well—our symmetrical response.”

news.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
news.summary: Study finds coding efficiency gains get "absorbed" by human review "bottleneck."
news.body:
Anyone who has even tangentially associated with computer programming knows that modern AI coding assistants and agents can be incredibly efficient at generating huge amounts of functional code . But coders making use of those tools also know better than to trust the accuracy of that code , meaning substantial effort needs to be spent reviewing any AI-generated output.

A recent study of actual coding practices across hundreds of firms finds that human code review forms a significant "bottleneck" for the overall efficiency of AI coding tools, resulting in "little evidence that firms increase software output or reduce employment" by using them. Any efficiency increased during the actual coding phase, the study authors find, is "absorbed by downstream constraints in the production process"; as "the code review process significantly increases in length, pull requests are more likely to require revisions, and reviewers leave more comments."

To come to these conclusions, Harvard University researchers Fiona Chen and James Stratton made use of aggregated analytics data from Jellyfish , which measures the granular output of engineering teams. That data encompasses 300 million individual "work events" (e.g., commits and pull requests) and issue management software data across more than 700,000 employees at over 700 relevant software development firms from 2021 through March of 2026.

news.title: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
news.summary: New winner is Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam for video of a roundworm and single-celled Dileptus.
news.body:
Last month we covered the winner of Nikon's Small World in Motion video: Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China, whose video captured tiny cilia beating in the airways of a child with a rare respiratory disorder. But allegations surfaced about Xu's use of AI while making the video. Nikon launched an investigation and concluded that Xu's entry did not comply with competition rules. The new winner is Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam with a video of a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism (above).

According to a BBC report, some researchers expressed concern that Xu's video had structural abnormalities and that cell features appeared and disappeared in a way one would not see in actual cellular biology. Others spotted what looked like AI watermarks embedded within the source files. Xu said he used AI “to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images”; however, he denied that AI was used "to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion.”

Founded in 2011, the Nikon Small World in Motion competition is a spinoff of the company’s Small World Photomicrography Competition, which has been around since 1974. Both are meant “to showcase the beauty and complexity of things seen through the light microscope”—one through still photographs, the other through photovideography, taking advantage of all the technological advances that now allow users to make movies or time-lapse images through the microscope.

The other winners also moved up a notch with Xu's disqualification. Benedikt Pleyer of Bavaria, Germany, placed second with a video of jellyfish larvae suspended in water droplets; Andrew Moore of Howard Hughes Medical Institute in the US placed third with a video of synchronized cell division in neighboring cells; Patrick Hickey of Hypha Research Ltd. in Edinburgh, Scotland, placed fourth with a video of the dynamics of mitochondria and chloroplasts in Turtle Vine leaf cells; and Igor Adameyko placed fifth with a video of a tiny, colorful sea slug ( Cyerce kikutarobabai ) on the move.

news.summary: Paperback is a fast, fully accessible reader for ebooks, documents and audio books. It opens over twenty formats and speaks sixteen languages. Opening documents: Use…
news.body:
Published 9 October 2026 by Quin

Paperback is a fast, fully accessible reader for ebooks, documents and audio books. It opens over twenty formats and speaks sixteen languages.

Opening documents:

Reading and listening:

Paperback has two ways to read a document. In text mode, you read the text with your screen reader. In read aloud mode, Paperback reads the text to you with the voice you pick in Settings, and keeps going in the background and from the lock screen. Switch between them from the More Options menu. Audio books, like DAISY, M4B, and MP3 books, play their own recording instead.

The reading bar:

The bar at the bottom of the screen has, from left to right:

You can also swipe up or down on the play button to move by the navigation unit, without reaching for the previous and next buttons. If that is all you use, the Hide previous and next buttons setting takes them out of your screen reader’s way. The Swipe up moves forward setting picks which way a swipe goes.

More options

The More Options menu is where everything else lives.

Keyboards and headsets:

With a keyboard, the desktop shortcuts for opening books, recent documents, Find, Go To, the table of contents, word count, document info, export, and the sleep timer all work. So do the single-letter keys for moving by heading, page, link, and the rest, and Space plays and pauses. A headset button plays and pauses with one press, moves forward with two, and goes back with three.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Paperback was designed with screen readers, and works flawlessly with both TalkBack and Backtalk.

news.title: IA visual directamente en el móvil: hacia una asistencia más privada y sin depender de la nube
news.summary: La inteligencia artificial visual puede convertirse en una herramienta cada vez más útil para las personas ciegas o con baja visión. Actualmente, muchas aplicaciones utilizan la cámara del teléfono para describir imágenes, reconocer objetos, leer textos o responder preguntas sobre lo que aparece delante del usuario. Sin embargo, habitualmente este procesamiento depende de servicios en […] La entrada IA visual directamente en el móvil: hacia una asistencia más privada y sin depender de la nube se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
La inteligencia artificial visual puede convertirse en una herramienta cada vez más útil para las personas ciegas o con baja visión. Actualmente, muchas aplicaciones utilizan la cámara del teléfono para describir imágenes, reconocer objetos, leer textos o responder preguntas sobre lo que aparece delante del usuario. Sin embargo, habitualmente este procesamiento depende de servicios en la nube.

En 2026, Envision, Arm y Google están explorando una alternativa: ejecutar modelos de inteligencia artificial visual directamente en el propio teléfono . El objetivo es que determinadas funciones puedan realizarse localmente, sin necesidad de enviar la imagen a servidores externos.

La tecnología se basa en Gemma 4 , la nueva familia de modelos de inteligencia artificial de Google. Entre sus capacidades se encuentra la comprensión de imágenes, que permite realizar tareas como describir una escena, reconocer elementos de una imagen, responder preguntas sobre su contenido o realizar razonamiento visual. Google indica que determinados modelos de Gemma 4 están diseñados para ejecutarse directamente en dispositivos móviles y otros equipos de computación local.

En colaboración con Arm, Envision ha probado esta tecnología para trasladar parte de sus funciones de comprensión visual al propio teléfono. En las pruebas descritas por Arm, el usuario puede capturar una fotografía y recibir una descripción detallada de la escena sin necesidad de enviar esa imagen a la nube ni disponer de conexión de red .

La colaboración aprovecha, además, las capacidades de los procesadores Arm y de Arm Scalable Matrix Extension 2 (SME2) , unas instrucciones diseñadas para acelerar determinadas operaciones relacionadas con inteligencia artificial. Según Arm, las pruebas iniciales con Gemma 4 muestran mejoras de rendimiento al ejecutar estas cargas de trabajo en procesadores Arm compatibles.

El funcionamiento local de la IA visual podría tener varias ventajas importantes para las tecnologías de apoyo.

Mayor privacidad. Si una imagen puede analizarse directamente en el teléfono, no es necesario enviar esa fotografía a un servidor externo para realizar el procesamiento. Esto puede ser especialmente relevante cuando la cámara está captando personas, documentos, espacios privados u otra información sensible.

Menor dependencia de Internet. Una IA que funciona en el propio dispositivo puede seguir ofreciendo determinadas funciones incluso cuando no existe conexión a Internet. Para una persona ciega o con baja visión, esto puede resultar especialmente interesante cuando utiliza herramientas de descripción visual fuera de casa o en lugares con una cobertura deficiente.

Menor latencia. El procesamiento local también puede reducir el tiempo necesario para obtener una respuesta, ya que la imagen no tiene que viajar hasta un servidor y regresar con el resultado. Arm señala precisamente una menor latencia y una mayor disponibilidad como algunos de los posibles beneficios de trasladar la inteligencia artificial al dispositivo.

La propuesta resulta especialmente interesante porque no se limita a obtener una descripción automática de una fotografía.

Envision plantea utilizar esta tecnología para funciones como la descripción de escenas y las preguntas y respuestas sobre información visual . En la práctica, una persona podría apuntar con la cámara del teléfono hacia un entorno, obtener una descripción y realizar posteriormente preguntas relacionadas con aquello que aparece en la imagen.

Este planteamiento parte de tecnologías que ya existen en Envision. Su aplicación permite actualmente utilizar la cámara del teléfono para describir escenas, reconocer objetos y responder preguntas sobre textos o imágenes mediante su asistente de inteligencia artificial. La diferencia de esta nueva línea de investigación está en dónde se realiza el procesamiento : el objetivo es llevar una parte cada vez mayor de esa comprensión visual al propio dispositivo.

Es importante aclarar que no estamos ante el lanzamiento de un nuevo producto de Envision que ya ofrezca todas estas funciones de forma general y completamente offline .

Envision, Arm y Google están trabajando en esta dirección y han mostrado un prototipo basado en Gemma 4 ejecutándose localmente en hardware Arm. Por tanto, se trata de una línea de desarrollo tecnológico , no de una característica que debamos considerar actualmente disponible en todos los teléfonos o en todas las funciones de Envision.

El avance, sin embargo, apunta hacia un cambio interesante en la evolución de las tecnologías de asistencia: que el teléfono no tenga que enviar continuamente lo que está viendo a la nube para poder comprenderlo .

Para las personas ciegas y con baja visión, esto podría traducirse en herramientas de asistencia visual más rápidas, privadas y capaces de funcionar en más situaciones, incluso cuando no exista conexión a Internet.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: Envision , Arm , Google deepmind .

news.title: Getting Started: Essential ZoomText and Fusion Features for the Workplace
news.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful …
news.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work. To help you get started, we’ll highlight some of the most important ZoomText and Fusion features that can make your daily work tasks easier and more efficient.

ZoomText and Fusion offer flexible magnification , letting you choose the level that works best for your tasks and environment. You can select from different zoom window types —like full screen, lens, or docked—and even use multiple monitors for expanded workspace. Advanced Smoothing, including xFont and Geometric Smoothing, keeps text and graphics sharp and easy to read at any magnification level.

Color Enhancements allow you to adjust color settings for better clarity. You can apply preset color schemes, switch to two-color modes, or replace specific problem colors to make on-screen content easier to see. These options help reduce eye strain, especially during long workdays.

Focus enhancements help you track your position in menus, dialogs, and application controls, so you never lose your place. Mouse pointers and cursors can be customized in size and color, making them easier to spot and follow on the screen.

AppReader is a built-in tool that reads documents, web pages, and emails aloud, supporting users who need to hear text read aloud. This is extremely useful for users who experience eye fatigue when reading long documents and emails.

For Fusion users, the full JAWS screen reader is included, adding speech and Braille support to all ZoomText magnification features. JAWS features like Say All (which reads from your cursor position), virtual cursor navigation for web pages and applications, and Quick Navigation keys for navigating web pages make workplace tasks more accessible. Fusion lets you switch seamlessly between magnification and speech, depending on your needs.

With ZoomText and Fusion, you can customize your environment to match your vision needs and adjust settings at any time as your tasks change. You can also save your personalized settings, so your preferred setup is always ready whenever you start your work day.

Stay tuned for Week 2, where we’ll explore how to use ZoomText and Fusion across your workday, from Microsoft Word to Teams, to help you stay productive and connected. We’ll discuss important ZoomText and Fusion settings, plus provide tips for navigating workplace apps with more confidence and ease.
